name: SCD40-D-R2
title: SCD4x: photoacoustic NDIR CO2 sensor with on-board humidity and temperature sensing, I2C output
summary: The SCD40 and SCD41 are reflow-solderable CO2 sensors in a 10.1 × 10.1 × 6.5 mm LGA module, measuring CO2 by photoacoustic NDIR and reporting 0 to 40'000 ppm over I2C at address 0x62. A humidity and temperature sensor inside the module compensates the CO2 reading and is read out as well. The module runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; it draws peaks above 100 mA, so the supply is sized for the peak. The SCD40 is specified from 400 to 2'000 ppm; the SCD41 is specified to 5'000 ppm with a tighter accuracy and adds an on-demand single-shot mode and a sleep state.
key_figures: 175 mA typ at 3.3 V, 115 mA typ at 5 V

rows: SCD41 mounted on a development board, with cables
adapter linking the SEK-SCD41-Sensor to a computer
notes: SCD40: base accuracy, specified from 400 to 2'000 ppm. SCD41: higher accuracy, specified from 400 to 5'000 ppm, with the single-shot commands. The SCD42 has a datasheet of its own.

rows: Additional accuracy drift per year with automatic self-calibration algorithm enabled (4)
notes: (1) With automatic self-calibration on, spells below 400 ppm CO2 can spoil the accuracy.

(2) Accuracy is the deviation from a high-precision reference, met by more than 90 % of sensors after calibration, using test gases of ± 1.5 % tolerance. Rough handling and shipping degrade it. Assembly degrades it for a while; FRC or ASC recalibration more than 5 days after assembly brings it fully back.
(3) Time to reach 63 % of a step, measured on the SCD41 evaluation kit in default measurement mode. In a product it depends on the design, the update rate and the surroundings.
(4) ASC needs the sensor to see 400 ppm air regularly. Stress tests put the worst-case drift per year at ± (5 ppm + 2 % of reading); mishandling can give more.

notes: (5) The humidity and temperature readings are affected by how the sensor is built in, by its self-heating and by its surroundings. circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor on an I2C bus. VDD and VDDH are tied together near the sensor and fed from the supply rail; GND goes to ground. Each bus line has a pull-up resistor Rp to the supply, 10 kΩ given as an example value; the host only pulls the lines low.
notes: The pull-ups can instead be those built into a microcontroller's I/O. Their value is chosen for the bus capacitance and clock rate.

operation.text: CO2 is measured by photoacoustic NDIR. A humidity and temperature sensor of the SHT4x family inside the module supplies the compensation, and its readings are output too.

VDD and VDDH come from the same supply and are joined close to the sensor. The supply should be quiet, with ripple under 30 mV peak to peak (an LDO is the suggested source), able to give the peak current, and free of large transient dips.
The sensor starts once VDD passes 2.25 V and takes 1000 ms to reach idle, after which it accepts commands.

Commands are 16-bit codes. Data are 16-bit unsigned words, most significant byte first, each followed by a CRC-8 byte. The host must send the CRC on writes; on reads checking it is optional. Every transfer opens with START and closes with STOP. In a read or a command with a result, the sensor acknowledges the read header only after the command's execution time, so the host waits that long before reading. A new command is not sent while one is still executing.

start_periodic_measurement makes the sensor measure with a new result every 5 s. Each result can be read once; reading empties the buffer, and a read with no new data is answered with a NACK. get_data_ready_status tells whether a result is waiting. The host may stop a read early with a NACK and STOP after any byte. While measuring, the sensor accepts four commands only: set_ambient_pressure, get_data_ready_status, read_measurement and stop_periodic_measurement. After stop_periodic_measurement the sensor ignores commands for 500 ms.
Settings are read and written in idle: stop the measurement, change settings, send persist_settings if they should survive a power cycle, then start measuring again.

The offset corrects the temperature and humidity outputs for heat inside the product and does not affect CO2. It depends on the measurement mode, nearby heat sources, ambient temperature and air flow. Default 4 °C.

Giving the sensor its altitude (default 0 m) or the ambient pressure compensates the CO2 reading for pressure. Altitude is set in idle, usually once at installation. set_ambient_pressure is accepted during measurement and takes precedence over the altitude setting; it suits places where the pressure changes much.

FRC sets the CO2 reading to a known reference at once, for example to remove the shift that assembly causes. Run the sensor for more than 3 minutes in the mode it will use, in steady and uniform CO2, at the supply voltage of the product; send stop_periodic_measurement and wait 500 ms; send perform_forced_recalibration with the reference concentration and, after 400 ms, read back the correction. The command fails if the sensor was not running beforehand.

ASC keeps the CO2 reading stable over the long term on its own, provided the sensor sees atmospheric CO2 of 400 ppm at least once a week. It is on by default, in single shot as well. It is tuned for single shots every 5 minutes; longer intervals calibrate less often, and power-cycling between shots stops it calibrating.
start_low_power_periodic_measurement gives a result about every 30 s. It uses less power and heats the sensor less, at the cost of a slower response; it is read like the default mode.

Temperature offset, altitude and the ASC setting live in RAM until persist_settings writes them to EEPROM; that EEPROM is rated for at least 2000 writes, so it is written only when a setting has actually changed. FRC and ASC history is saved automatically in a separate EEPROM sized for the sensor's life.
get_serial_number returns a unique 48-bit number, which also confirms the sensor is present. perform_self_test checks the sensor and its supply, for example at the end of a production line.
perform_factory_reset clears the stored settings and the FRC and ASC history. reinit reloads settings from EEPROM and is sent after stopping measurement; if it does not take effect, cycle the power.

On the SCD41, measure_single_shot makes one measurement on request (5000 ms), read with read_measurement; measure_single_shot_rht_only (50 ms) measures only humidity and temperature and reports CO2 as 0 ppm. Averaging several shots lowers the noise. The first shot after power-up or after wake_up is discarded. Between shots the sensor idles at 0.15 mA typ (0.2 mA max); one shot takes 243 mJ typ (296 mJ max).
power_down puts the idle sensor to sleep. wake_up returns it to idle but is not acknowledged; reading the serial number confirms it is awake.
The white membrane on top must stay in place and untouched. The module weighs about 0.6 g.
MSL 3 to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-033B1. Floor time out of the bag is 168 h at no more than 30 °C and 60 % RH; past that, after hotter or damper exposure, or with a doubtful dry pack, the sensors are baked.

Reflow to J-STD-020 with a peak of 235 °C for up to 30 s. The sensor is large enough that its cap can be hotter than the pads, and no part of it may pass 235 °C. No vapour-phase reflow, no board wash afterwards, and the dust cover is kept dry and in place. Reflow can shift the CO2 reading slightly; full accuracy returns within five days, powered or not.
Each sensor carries an electronic serial number; only Sensirion can decode it to the sensor's production, calibration and test records.
REACH and RoHS compliant.
